arXiv:2603.02316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a variational wave function based on Neural-Network Quantum States (NQS) to study lattice systems whose local Hilbert space contains both spin and fermionic degrees of freedom. 👤 Marcel F. Langer, Adrian Hill, Michele Ceriotti
arXiv:2609.20510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) learn the mapping from atomic positions to potential energy. The forces, the negative gradient of this energy, drive molecular dynamics and are readily obtained using automatic differentiation. Higher-order derivatives, most notably the Hessian, describe collective motion and allow the direct prediction of experimental observables, but are considered computationally inaccessible for large systems. We suggest a solution: in physical systems, interactions decay with distance, and most MLIPs build on this locality through message passing up to a finite receptive field. We develop a hierarchical GP potential combining physics-informed priors with Bayesian propagation of hyperparameter uncertainty that retains useful discrimination of prediction errors while remaining conservative rather than overconfident, with a probabilistic structure that allows the sources of predictive uncertainty to be explicitly dissected. item.title: A Physics-First Hamiltonian Latent Model for Twelve Universality Classes of Fluid Behaviour
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Lucas Lima Freitag
We present Fluido Universal (FU), a physics-first, purely analytic reduced-order framework that reproduces eighteen universal indicators of fluid behaviour across twelve distinct physical regimes—from wall-bounded turbulence to superfluid helium, from rarefied Martian CO2 to solar-wind plasma. Unlike data-driven closures (e.g. graph neural networks, WMLES with embedded ML, PINNs), FU contains no learned parameters, no autoencoder, and no sparseregression step: every indicator is either a closed-form algebraic law or a first-principles ODE integrated by a fourth-order Runge–Kutta scheme, using only CODATA 2022 constants. The framework is embedded in an interactive WebGL2 Navier–Stokes solver that runs on consumer hardware and validates all eighteen indicators live. The eighteen indicators…

📚 arXiv
👤 Yogendra Limbu, Michael E. Flatté, Durga Paudyal
arXiv:2609.20616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antiferromagnetic oxides offer a compelling paradigm for magnonics. Combining ab initio and spin Hamiltonian modeling, we map Cr2O3 from bulk to monolayer limits, verifying stability via phonon spectra. Contrary to previously predicted half-metallic ferromagnetic monolayer phases, we conclusively demonstrate that monolayer and bilayer configurations preserve an antiferromagnetic semiconductor ground state despite systematic gap narrowing. Intersecting magnon and phonon branches drive strong hybridization, establishing low-dimensional Cr2O3 as an ideal platform for quantum spintronics.
